title: auth: unify header semantics for project/org keys, scoped tokens, CORS, and request signing
author: Priya Nair
description: Motivation: We have several inconsistent auth header semantics across the Redwood API surface and the OpenAI-compat layer: project vs org-scoped keys, header name differences (Authorization vs X-Redwood-Project), scoped/session tokens, CORS preflight handling, and a prototype request-signing nonce header. This PR unifies the contract and documents migration steps.
commits: feat(auth): introduce x-redwood-project and standardize Authorization precedence
feat(tokens): add scoped token validation and token-type header mapping
fix(cors): ensure preflight exposes X-Redwood-Project and X-RW-Signature headers
chore(docs): update openai-compat header semantics and migration guide
test(auth): add unit and integration tests for precedence and signing
review_comments: Evan Clark: Overall looks good. Two requests: 1) make precedence explicit in the code comments (Authorization -> X-Redwood-Scoped-Token -> X-Redwood-Project), 2) make sure legacy project header fallback is opt-in behind feature flag for Dedicated customers.
Priya Nair: Responding: added explicit precedence table in headers.go and added RW_FEATURE_LEGACY_PROJECT_HEADER flag gated by customer config; tests added to cover flag behavior.
Jordan Liu: Security question: how are we preventing replay attacks with the nonce header? Can tests simulate clock skew?
Priya Nair: Added nonce window of 2 minutes configurable via RW_SIGNING_WINDOW and unit tests that simulate clock skew +/-3 minutes; verified rejected outside window.

Maya Patel: Docs nit: update openai-compat doc to call out that Authorization bearer tokens with scope:project will map to X-Redwood-Project automatically. Also ensure CORS preflight exposes X-RW-Signature.
Priya Nair: Done; docs updated and e2e scenario added that runs a browser-like preflight check in CI.
merge_commit_message:
auth: unify header semantics for project/org keys, scoped tokens, CORS, and request signing

Includes header precedence, scoped-token support, CORS preflight exposure, nonce signing verification and docs/migration guide.
release_notes: Unify auth headers: Authorization precedence documented; add X-Redwood-Project and X-Redwood-Scoped-Token handling; CORS preflights now expose auth-related headers; request-signing nonce validation added. Migration guide: docs/migration/2026-02-auth-unify.md
